subject.title: Gateway becomes slow or times out under multi-session / multi-agent load

question: Should this issue remain the broad live-workload Gateway liveness tracker, or should maintainers narrow it to one remaining storage/default-policy issue and close the umbrella?
rationale: The code already contains several partial hot-path fixes, but the remaining behavior spans multiple owner boundaries and needs maintainer scoping plus live proof rather than a single obvious code repair.

options.title: Keep Broad Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for current-main live reproduction and end-to-end Gateway liveness proof while linking narrower transcript/default-policy issues as partial overlaps.

options.title: Narrow To Transcript Policy
options.body: Declare the remaining user-visible problem to be raw active transcript growth/default policy and close this issue after moving all evidence to the canonical transcript issues.

options.title: Sponsor Reliability Project
options.body: Turn this into a maintainer-owned Gateway reliability project covering handler metrics, backpressure, storage/indexing, and channel-delivery load testing.

recommendation.title: Keep Broad Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for current-main live reproduction and end-to-end Gateway liveness proof while linking narrower transcript/default-policy issues as partial overlaps.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent release/current-main provenance and coauthorship on the adjacent sessions.list concurrency fix make this the best available routing candidate from the inspected history.
